cards.text: Paul is writing to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2), and he's just been setting them straight about how they gather (1 Corinthians 11:17-34). Now he turns a corner: "Now about spiritual gifts, brothers, I do not want you to be uninformed." Friend, I spent YEARS uninformed in the back of a junk drawer, so I am leaning ALL the way in on this one.

cards.question: Paul reminds the Corinthians what life looked like back when they were pagans. What does he say they were led astray to?

cards.text: Idols that never say a word, like asking for directions and getting a blank STARE. So Paul gives them a way to tell when someone is really speaking by the Spirit of God.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says a person speaking by the Spirit of God can say Jesus should be cursed.
Now the flip side. According to Paul, who makes it possible for anyone to say Jesus is Lord?

cards.text: Paul gets a rhythm going: different gifts, but the same Spirit, and different ministries, but the same Lord. I'm over here nodding along like it's my favorite song on the radio.

cards.question: Then comes the third line of Paul's rhythm: There are different ways of working, but the same ___ works all things in all people.

cards.text: Now Paul says something about every single believer in that church. Nobody's stuck in the back of the drawer on this one, friend.

cards.question: To each one the manifestation of the ___ is given for the common ___.

cards.text: Then Paul starts listing gifts: one person gets the message of wisdom, another the message of knowledge, another faith, all by the same Spirit. Same oven, different batches, friend.

cards.question: True or false: gifts of healing are on Paul's list of gifts too.

cards.text: Miracles! Prophecy! Distinguishing between spirits! Tongues AND interpreting tongues! And Paul says every one of them is the work of one and the same Spirit.

cards.question: One Spirit and all those different gifts. So how does each person end up with the gift they get?

answers.text: The Spirit gives as He determines
Each person picks the one they want
The church leaders hand them out

cards.text: Now Paul grabs a picture everybody's got: the body, one unit made of many parts. And believe me, a stamper who uses his MUSTACHE for hands has thought a LOT about body parts.

cards.question: Paul says the body is one unit made of many parts. Who does he say is just like that?

cards.text: Then Paul says how people come into this one body: in one Spirit, by being baptized into it, and by being given one Spirit to drink.

cards.question: True or false: Paul says Jews and Greeks, slave and free, were all baptized into that one body.

cards.text: The body isn't one part, it's many. Then Paul gives the foot a voice, and it says, "Because I am not a hand, I do not belong to the body," and friend, I spent years in a junk drawer feeling EXACTLY like that foot.

cards.question: True or false: when the foot says it doesn't belong because it isn't a hand, that makes it less a part of the body.

cards.text: Then the ear tries it: "Because I am not an eye, I do not belong to the body," and Paul gives it the same answer he gave the foot. Meanwhile I'm picturing the hand and the eye just looking at each other like, why are WE in this?

cards.question: Paul pictures the whole body as one giant eye, and then as one giant ear. What's his point?

answers.text: A body needs all its different parts
The eye is the most important part
The other parts should copy the eye

cards.question: So how did all the parts of the body end up where they are? Who does Paul say arranged every one of them?

answers.text: Each part by its own choice
The strongest part of the body

cards.text: If every part were the same part, Paul asks, where would the body even be? As it is, many parts, one body, because a cookie that's ALL sprinkles isn't a cookie, friend, it's just a pile of sprinkles.

cards.question: Now Paul looks at it from the other side. The eye cannot say to the hand, I do not ___ you.
True or false: Paul says the parts of the body that seem weaker can be done without.

cards.text: Paul says the parts we consider less honorable get treated with greater honor, and God has given greater honor to the parts that lacked it. And as the stamper who got called out of the back of a drawer, let me tell you, I am a BIG fan of that.

cards.question: Why does Paul say God put the body together that way?

answers.text: So there would be no division in the body
So the strong parts could lead the rest
So each part could work on its own

cards.question: Paul says the parts of the body are tied together: If one part suffers, every part ___ with it; if one part is honored, every part ___ with it.

cards.text: Then Paul lands it: "Now you are the body of Christ, and each of you is a member of it." Next he lists what God has appointed in the church, and number two is prophets, number three is teachers, then miracle workers, healing, helping, administration and various tongues.

cards.question: So who's at the top of Paul's list? In the church, God has appointed first of all ___.
Then Paul fires off questions: Are all apostles? Are all teachers? Do all speak in tongues? Do all interpret? What answer is he pointing to?

answers.text: No not everyone has every gift
Yes everyone should have them all
Only leaders should have them all

cards.question: True or false: after all those questions, Paul tells the Corinthians to eagerly desire the greater gifts.

cards.text: Then Paul says, "And now I will show you the most excellent way." Friend, I'm leaning in so far my chef's hat is about to slide off, but Paul's teaching isn't done yet, so we'll pick it up right there next time.

findings.problem: Paul appears here for the first time, but the card never says who he is. It only says he is writing to the church in Corinth. Add a short identifier, such as Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus (1 Corinthians 1:1).

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The joke "I'm over here nodding along like it's my favorite song on the radio" is mild and pleasant, not a real laugh. Stop 1 leans on gentle lines like this one, so this is the clearest place to push the humor further.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: This two-blank card reproduces 12:7 word for word and asks the baker to supply the wording. The second blank ("good" against "people") tests the phrase "common good," which the baker hasn't seen. The meaning can't settle it, because "for the common people" reads naturally too. Card 8 gives no context that points to either word. Ask about the meaning instead, for example why each one is given a manifestation of the Spirit.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card says "how people come into this one body" happens "by being given one Spirit to drink." Verse 13 lists being baptized into one body and being given one Spirit to drink side by side. It never says the drinking is how people enter the body. The card adds a connection the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 11 asks whether one item, gifts of healing, appears in the list of gifts in 12:8-10. Stop 2 card 17 likewise asks for the first item in the list in 12:28. These are list-membership details. The docs say a long stretch, including name lists, never gets a choice card. They also say teaching is not a long stretch. A list of gifts inside Paul's teaching falls between those two rules.
findings.question: When a list sits inside teaching (the gift lists in 1 Corinthians 12:8-10 and 12:28), does it count as a long stretch that gets one summary story card and no choice cards? Or is it teaching, so questions about items in the list are allowed?
